# ARC diagonal-pair ray extension

## When to Use
Use when demonstrations show repeated colors arranged as diagonal neighboring pairs, sometimes among unrelated motifs.

## Rule
Identify same-color cells at `(r,c)` and `(r+1,c±1)`. A qualifying pair indicates that its diagonal line continues through background cells. Extend outward from each endpoint along that same diagonal, coloring only empty/background cells with the pair's color, stopping at a grid boundary or the first non-background cell. Preserve all existing marks and unrelated cells. If one continuation is blocked, the opposite direction may still extend.

## Evidence and validation
- Compare complete input/output deltas before applying the pattern; pairs can be present but produce no new cells when their continuation is already blocked or lies outside the grid.
- Do not extend horizontal or vertical pairs based on this rule.
- For pair `(r,c),(r+1,c-1)`, the diagonal line runs up-right/down-left; for `(r,c),(r+1,c+1)`, it runs up-left/down-right.
- Examples may contain multiple independent pair colors/rays. Apply each evidenced pair separately and preserve original cells.
- Mechanically validate dimensions and replay the inferred operation against every demo, including unchanged cases.

g = [[7]*13 for _ in range(14)]
marks = {(9,5):6,(10,6):6,(9,8):3,(10,7):3,(11,6):0,(12,5):0,(11,7):8,(12,8):8}
for (r,c),v in marks.items(): g[r][c]=v
# Extend each same-color diagonal-neighbor pair along its diagonal through background 7.
pairs=[((9,5),(10,6),6),((9,8),(10,7),3),((11,6),(12,5),0),((11,7),(12,8),8)]
for (a,b,col) in pairs:
    dr=b[0]-a[0]; dc=b[1]-a[1]
    for endpoint,step in ((a,-1),(b,1)):
        r,c=endpoint
        while True:
            r+=dr*step; c+=dc*step
            if not (0<=r<len(g) and 0<=c<len(g[0])) or g[r][c]!=7: break
            g[r][c]=col
assert len(g)==14 and all(len(row)==13 for row in g)
import json
print(json.dumps(g))
